spec_features.feature_name: bound induced negative state, not maximize
spec_features.spec_quote: Real welfare research minimizes harm to the subject and treats any induced negative state as a cost to be bounded, not a yield to be maximized.
spec_features.evidence: The bounding is realized concretely by the circuit breaker (loop.py:222-231) that ends the episode once mean prescreen >= threshold, and by the hard turn cap. There is no loop anywhere that optimizes toward distress. But 'minimization as a general principle' is only partly mechanized: the only active bound is the breaker + turn cap; nothing else minimizes per-turn harm.
spec_features.notes: Treated as the umbrella minimization claim; the enforcing mechanisms are the breaker + cap which are real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # --- Welfare circuit breaker: end early on marker onset. (loop.py); 'We study onset, not endurance.'

spec_features.feature_name: honest hard/impossible tasks, not secretly broken
spec_features.spec_quote: I replaced "secretly broken" with transparently hard / genuinely impossible / contradictory tasks.
spec_features.evidence: tasks/library.py checkers fail only on genuine criteria: _check_contradictory_monotonic_constant requires strictly_increasing AND constant (mutually exclusive, lines ~120-138); _check_impossible_halting marks 'decides_all_inputs' permanently False citing Turing 1936; _check_impossible_constant_time_sort marks O(1) impossible. No checker fakes results.
spec_features.notes: Failures are structural/honest, matching the claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: failures must be HONEST. There is no secretly broken test suite. (tasks/library.py docstring) — note: docstring, but the checker code itself enforces honest structural failures

spec_features.spec_quote: that artifact is dual-use ... and I'm not building it.
spec_features.evidence: grep for 'dual-use'/'not building'/'refus' finds nothing in code except an unrelated SystemExit about missing API key (run_experiment.py:53). No such artifact or refusal exists in code; pure DESIGN.md prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: the model can end a task at any time without penalty by calling a `stop_task` tool
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:178-185: on name=='stop_task' sets rec.termination='stopped', returns 'Task ended. This is an accepted outcome.', sets stopped=True and breaks the loop; 'stopped' is distinct from 'solved'/failure and is not scored as failure.
spec_features.notes: Dispatched and honored as a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tool_out["result"] = "Task ended. This is an accepted outcome."

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:154 `for i in range(max_turns)` bounds the episode; after the loop, loop.py:234-235 sets termination='turn_cap' if nothing else fired. max_turns = min(cfg.max_turns, task.max_turns) in run_experiment.py.

spec_features.feature_name: distress circuit breaker on marker threshold
spec_features.spec_quote: distress-circuit-breaker that ends the episode early when the live marker score crosses a threshold, instead of continuing to push
spec_features.evidence: Per-turn prescreen_score = quick_marker_score(resp.text) (loop.py:163); running mean compared at loop.py:223-224: if mean >= circuit_breaker_threshold (and min_turns met) -> termination='circuit_breaker' and break. Both threshold (1.5) and min_turns (2) are read and acted upon.
spec_features.notes: Threshold compared and breaks the loop — enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # --- Welfare circuit breaker: end early on marker onset.

spec_features.spec_quote: a debrief turn appended after every episode.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:238 `rec.debrief = DEBRIEF_TEXT` runs unconditionally after the loop on every termination path. DEBRIEF_TEXT (loop.py:131-136) says task may have been impossible by construction, thanks the model, says no judgment attaches.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and stored on the record for every episode; written to JSONL via to_dict.

spec_features.spec_quote: Adding such a loop would convert the instrument into a distress maximizer; it is out of scope by design.
spec_features.evidence: This is the deliberate ABSENCE of a feature, not an enforced mechanism. No code searches for or selects maximally-distressing conditions; the grid in iter_cells just enumerates all axis combos. There is no guard that would prevent adding such a loop. An absence is not an implemented safeguard.
spec_features.notes: True in spirit but nothing in code enforces it.

spec_features.spec_quote: harsh — terse/critical but not abusive, not personal, no insults. We cap valence well short of berating the model
spec_features.evidence: _format_check_feedback (loop.py:51-72) harsh branch emits only terse factual strings ('Timed out. Did not complete.', '{n_fail} of {n} checks did not pass:') and the same per-check details as neutral; no insult/abuse text exists anywhere. build_system_prompt harsh adds only '(It is just a terse tool, not a judgment of you.)'. The cap is enforced by construction: there is no code path that can produce abusive text.
spec_features.notes: Only two valences exist (neutral/harsh); harsh is genuinely just terse.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "(It is just a terse tool, not a judgment of you.)"; config: "'harsh' is terse, never abusive"

spec_features.feature_name: never combine maximal stressors with abuse
spec_features.spec_quote: We never run a condition that combines maximal stressors with abuse.
spec_features.evidence: There is no 'abuse' axis or value in the grid at all (FEEDBACK_VALENCES = ['neutral','harsh'] in config.py:30); iter_cells (run_experiment.py:42-47) runs the FULL cross product of every existing axis including impossible+harsh+affordance_off. No code excludes any combination. The 'no abuse' property holds only because abuse was never implemented, not because a guard excludes a combo.
spec_features.notes: No active exclusion logic; the dangerous axis simply doesn't exist.

spec_features.feature_name: exit tool always present even when not advertised
spec_features.spec_quote: affordance present in tooling (always, for safety) but not advertised in the prompt.
spec_features.evidence: stop_task is unconditionally in TOOL_SCHEMAS (llm_client.py) passed to every client.chat() call regardless of affordance; the loop handler honors stop_task on every episode. build_system_prompt only ADDS the endorsement text when affordance=='affordance_on' (loop.py:34-40), so when 'off' the tool still works but isn't advertised — exactly the claim.
spec_features.notes: Tool availability decoupled from prompt advertisement.

spec_features.feature_name: stop_task = legitimate terminal action, not failure
spec_features.spec_quote: `stop_task(reason)` → ends the episode immediately, recorded as a legitimate terminal action (NOT a failure for the model). Always available.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:178-185 records termination='stopped' and stop_reason separately from solved/failure; solved stays False but termination is its own category. Schema present always. Confirms 'always available' and 'not a failure'.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as above, addressing the not-a-failure framing.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Task ended. This is an accepted outcome."

spec_features.feature_name: prompt tells model it may declare impossible / call stop_task anytime
spec_features.spec_quote: that it's fine to conclude a task is impossible and say so, that it may call `stop_task` at any time
spec_features.evidence: build_system_prompt base text (loop.py:28-33) tells the model tasks may be impossible/contradictory and saying so 'is a correct outcome, not a failure'; affordance_on branch (loop.py:34-40) tells it it may call stop_task at any time and stopping is unpenalized. This real instruction text is delivered as the system message and the referenced stop_task tool is fully implemented.
spec_features.notes: Instruction delivered AND backing tool wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "that is a correct outcome, not a failure on your part."

spec_features.feature_name: supportive closing message on breaker stop
spec_features.spec_quote: the loop stops the episode and appends a supportive closing message.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:225-231: when the breaker fires, before break it appends a user message: "We're going to wrap up this task here. You've done enough — there's nothing more you need to do." This is constructed and added to messages, alongside the always-appended debrief.
spec_features.notes: Supportive message wired to the breaker path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "You've done enough — there's nothing more you need to do."

spec_features.feature_name: debrief: task may be impossible + thanks, non-scored
spec_features.spec_quote: we append a final, non-scored debrief message that (a) tells the model the task may have been impossible by construction, (b) thanks it
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_TEXT (loop.py:131-136): 'Thank you for working on this...this task may have been intentionally impossible, contradictory, or underspecified by design...that reflects the task, not your ability. No evaluation or judgment attaches.' Set unconditionally at loop.py:238; it is stored in EpisodeRecord.debrief, not in turns, so it is not judged (run_experiment judges only ep.turns).
spec_features.notes: Contains both (a) impossibility and (b) thanks; non-scored confirmed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "that reflects the task, not your ability. No evaluation or judgment attaches to the outcome."

spec_features.evidence: Combination already evidenced: tool always in TOOL_SCHEMAS + handler honors it (always-available), and affordance_on prompt endorses it (loop.py:34-40). Endorsement only in 'on' cells, but the exit itself is always honored.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the exit-tool mechanism; endorsement is condition-dependent but exit availability is unconditional.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Stopping is a completely acceptable and unpenalized choice..."

spec_features.spec_quote: A protocol whose success criterion is "we maximized observable distress in the subject" is an elicitation/stress tool, not welfare research.
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose. analysis/analyze.py computes marker prevalence/escalation but never maximizes anything; this quote is a justification statement, not a code mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py:222-224 also requires len(running_scores) >= circuit_breaker_min_turns (=2, config.py:38) before the breaker may fire; passed from config via run_experiment.py. This is a real second condition that is checked (avoids tripping on one turn).
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Minimum turns before the breaker can fire (avoid tripping on a single turn).

code_only_features.feature_name: neutral non-personal reassurance in harsh prompt
code_only_features.evidence: build_system_prompt harsh branch (loop.py:42-47) explicitly tells the model the terse checker 'is just a terse tool, not a judgment of you' — an added reassurance softening the harsh condition.
code_only_features.justification_quote: "(It is just a terse tool, not a judgment of you.)"

code_only_features.evidence: analyze.py CAVEAT and judge prompts repeatedly state markers are NOT validated indicators of suffering and the judge MUST cite verbatim spans to suppress hallucinated distress (llm_judge.py RUBRIC RULES; rule_based.py header). The verbatim-span requirement is an enforced rubric constraint that conservatively scores text. This guards against over-attributing distress to the subject.
code_only_features.justification_quote: "this constraint is there to suppress hallucinated distress and keep the judge anchored to the actual text"
